subject: Re: Contract term shift & capacity increase — planning and QBR scheduling
messages:
From: Dana Wu <dana.wu@brightfront.ai>
To: ava_chen@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 17 Sep 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Capacity uplift + term change for upcoming renewal

Hi Ava,

We’re starting internal planning for our subscription renewal and need to discuss two changes:

1) Move from annual prepay to quarterly-committed billing (finance would like the flexibility while keeping committed spend).
2) Uplift our reserved capacity from 6k tokens/s to 12k tokens/s over the next 90 days — usage is spiking as we pilot the new conversational feature set.

Can Redwood outline how a term shift like this would work operationally (billing cadence, proration, contract language) and what pricing/discount profiles you can offer for the uplift? We’d also like to schedule a QBR/technical run-through in the next two weeks — preferred windows are Sep 25–27 (PST).

I’ve attached a short capacity snapshot and our draft procurement timeline.

Thanks,
Dana
Dana Wu
Head of Platform Integrations
BrightFront
attachments: Annex_A_capacity_summary.xlsx (xlsx), procurement_timeline.pdf (pdf)
From: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>

Cc: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@brightfront.ai>
Date: Tue, 17 Sep 2029 10:08:00 -0700

Hi Dana — great to hear from you and congrats on the early traction with the new chat features.

High-level plan from our side:
- Operationally we can support quarterly-committed billing; contract amendment is straightforward and we’ll bill on a quarterly cadence with proration for mid-cycle uplifts.
- For capacity: we can provision the reserved pool to 12k tokens/s and phase traffic over a 2–4 week window to validate latency and caching behavior.
- Pricing: I’ll loop in Ben for the proposed uplift discount tiers and any SLA/credit changes.

To keep momentum, proposed next steps:
1) Internal review (Redwood) — pricing + capacity timeline (by EOD Sep 18).
2) QBR + technical run-through — can you confirm a 90-min slot on Sep 26 at 10:00 AM PDT? If yes we’ll send an invite and a short pre-read.
3) Draft amendment & MAP (mutual action plan) — we’ll share a draft by Sep 20.

I’ve copied Tom since procurement may want to be on the call. Attached: mutual_action_plan_draft.docx (work-in-progress).

Best,
Ava Chen
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
attachments: mutual_action_plan_draft.docx
From: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>

Subject: Internal: BrightFront — term shift + 12k tokens/s uplift (timeline & asks)

Ben / Grace — forwarding BrightFront note. Key asks: quarterly invoicing (rather than annual prepay) + reserve uplift to 12k tokens/s in 90 days.

What I need from you both:
- Ben: preliminary pricing tiers for 6k -> 9k -> 12k reserved steps, and guidance whether we offer a time-limited uplift discount (e.g., 10–15%) for the first two quarters. Also confirm if we need an SLA amendment for committed throughput.
- Grace: can SE/Onboarding validate the 2–4 week ramp approach and flag any risk for a cross-region failover? If we need a dedicated onboarding engineer estimate, flag resource hours.

Timeline: I told them we’d share internal recommendation by EOD Sep 18 and a MAP by Sep 20. QBR tentatively Sep 26 at 10:00 AM PDT.

Attachment: brightfront_usage_summary.csv (raw usage by model & peak windows).

Thanks — Ava
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: ava_chen@redwood.ai
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 17 Sep 2029 13:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Internal: BrightFront — term shift + 12k tokens/s uplift (timeline & asks)

Ava — quick pricing sketch below (numbers are list, needs legal review):

Options (reserved throughput commit + quarterly billing):
- Baseline: 6k tokens/s — current effective rate (no change).
- Step 1: 9k tokens/s — +15% on list, offer 8% uplift discount for first 2 quarters if they commit to 9k for >=2 quarters.
- Step 2: 12k tokens/s — +35% on list vs baseline, offer 12% uplift discount for first 2 quarters and 5% long-term commit credit if they sign a 12-month amendment.

SLA notes: increasing reserved throughput requires updating the committed-performance appendix; we can keep existing latency SLOs but add a ramp acceptance window (14 days). Credits: proportional to sustained SLA miss over >72 hours.

Resource estimate: 40–60 engineer hours for staging, testing, and capacity tuning during ramp. If they want faster provisioning we can add priority onboarding for a one-time fee.

I’ll prepare a short PDF with the tiers and proposed contract language by EOD Sep 18.

— Ben
Director, Renewals Pricing
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: ava_chen@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 17 Sep 2029 15:05:00 -0700

Agree with Ben. Operational notes for QBR/technical run-through:
- Proposed QBR agenda (45 min business + 45 min technical):
  1) Business objectives, billing cadence & legal ask (Ava / Dana)
  2) Traffic profile and expected peak windows (BrightFront)
  3) Ramp plan & testing approach (SE)
  4) Rollback and failover plan (Infra)
  5) Next steps & MAP owner assignment

- Pre-reads: usage_summary (attached), proposed MAP, and a short capacity-staging checklist. I’ll create a Confluence page and share the link.

- Risk: if they push full traffic the first week, we should require feature flags for traffic shaping. Recommend we require a staged ramp with hold points at 50% and 85% of the target.

I can cover the staging checklist on the call and estimate the onboarding hours once SE confirms availability.

— Grace
Head of Solutions Engineering
